import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [
        1981, 1982, 1983, 1984, 1985,
        1981, 1982, 1983, 1984, 1985,
        1981, 1982, 1983, 1984, 1985,
        1981, 1982, 1983, 1984, 1985,
        1981, 1982, 1983, 1984, 1985,
        1981, 1982, 1983, 1984, 1985
    ],
    'Category': [
        'Debt Relief Programs', 'Debt Relief Programs', 'Debt Relief Programs', 'Debt Relief Programs', 'Debt Relief Programs',
        'Humanitarian Aid', 'Humanitarian Aid', 'Humanitarian Aid', 'Humanitarian Aid', 'Humanitarian Aid',
        'Roads & Railways', 'Roads & Railways', 'Roads & Railways', 'Roads & Railways', 'Roads & Railways',
        'Vocational Training', 'Vocational Training', 'Vocational Training', 'Vocational Training', 'Vocational Training',
        'Foreign Investments', 'Foreign Investments', 'Foreign Investments', 'Foreign Investments', 'Foreign Investments',
        'Agricultural Support', 'Agricultural Support', 'Agricultural Support', 'Agricultural Support', 'Agricultural Support'
    ],
    'Funding': [
        2200, 2450, 2700, 2900, 3100,
        310, 350, 390, 430, 480,
        650, 720, 800, 870, 950,
        880, 950, 1020, 1100, 1190,
        4600, 5000, 5400, 5800, 6200,
        950, 1030, 1120, 1200, 1300
    ],
    'Economic_Stability_Index': [
        5.2, 5.1, 4.9, 4.7, 4.5,
        5.8, 5.7, 5.5, 5.4, 5.2,
        5.5, 5.4, 5.2, 5.0, 4.8,
        5.7, 5.6, 5.4, 5.2, 5.0,
        4.9, 5.0, 5.1, 5.2, 5.4,
        5.3, 5.2, 5.0, 4.9, 4.7
    ],
    'Inflation_Rate': [
        28.7, 30.1, 32.0, 33.5, 35.0,
        27.5, 28.8, 29.5, 30.5, 31.8,
        26.8, 27.6, 28.5, 29.5, 31.0,
        27.9, 28.7, 29.6, 30.5, 31.8,
        30.1, 29.5, 28.8, 28.0, 27.2,
        27.2, 28.0, 28.8, 29.7, 30.5
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=len(df['Category'].unique()))

g = sns.lineplot(
    data=df,
    x='Year',
    y='Funding',
    hue='Category',
    style='Category',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    palette=palette,
    linewidth=2.5,
    legend=False
)

g.set_title('Financial Flows and Economic Trends in Mexico (1981-1985) by Program', fontsize=14, pad=20)
g.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=12)
g.set_ylabel('Funding (Millions USD)', fontsize=12)
g.legend(title='Program Category', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.gca().set_ylim(15.5, 6000)
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight')

SUMMARY:
 This image is a line chart titled "Financial Flows and Economic Trends in Mexico (1981-1985) by Program," which illustrates the annual funding allocations across different program categories over a five-year period. The chart features six distinct lines, each representing a specific program category, with funding amounts displayed on the vertical axis in millions of U.S. dollars and years on the horizontal axis.

The "Foreign Investments" program, represented by a bright blue line, consistently receives the highest funding, starting at 4,600 million USD in 1981 and rising steadily each year to 6,200 million USD by 1985. The "Debt Relief Programs," shown in red, also see significant funding, beginning at 2,200 million USD in 1981 and increasing to 3,100 million USD by 1985.

The "Agricultural Support" program is depicted with a purple line and shows a gradual increase from 950 million USD in 1981 to 1,300 million USD in 1985. "Vocational Training," illustrated with a teal line, starts at 880 million USD in 1981 and grows to 1,190 million USD by 1985. The "Roads & Railways" category, marked by a green line, receives funding that increases from 650 million USD in 1981 to 950 million USD in 1985. Lastly, "Humanitarian Aid," represented by a brown line, has the lowest funding amounts, starting at 310 million USD in 1981 and rising to 480 million USD by 1985.

Each line is accompanied by markers indicating the specific data points for each year, allowing for clear visualization of trends over time. The chart's gridlines provide additional context for interpreting the values, and the legend on the right clearly identifies each program category by both color and line style.

p = Path("chart.py")
source = p.read_text()
source = source.replace("legend=False", "legend=True")
source = source.replace("plt.gca().set_ylim(15.5, 6000)", "plt.gca().set_ylim(15.5, 6500)")
p.write_text(source)
exec(compile(source, "chart.py", "exec"))
ax = plt.gca()
print("Y limits:", ax.get_ylim())
print("Legend entries:", [t.get_text() for t in ax.get_legend().get_texts()])
print("Funding range:", df["Funding"].min(), df["Funding"].max())
print("Title:", ax.get_title())
